data.source_setting: AAOS/ASSH evidence-based guideline for acute distal-radius fracture care in adults age 18 and older.
data.source_n: Systematic review recommendation; no single cohort denominator.
data.quantity: Post-reduction alignment thresholds associated with improved outcomes after operative treatment in non-geriatric adults
data.source_evidence_basis: The guideline states moderate evidence supports operative treatment for non-geriatric patients meeting any listed post-reduction threshold, with improved radiographic and patient-reported outcomes.
data.limitations: Thresholds are decision support, not an autonomous rule; functional demand and patient preference matter. Derived from heterogeneous studies; not a locally validated RWJ protocol.
data.inferred_scenario_use: After radiographs following reduction, use these values to structure clinician discussion for an adult under 65; do not automatically turn threshold crossing into surgery.

data.source_title: Management of Distal Radius Fractures: Evidence-Based Clinical Practice Guideline
data.locator: Indications for Fixation (Geriatric Patients), PDF p.25, lines 318-323; future research, p.33, lines 367-375.
data.source_setting: AAOS/ASSH guideline for acute adult distal-radius fractures.
data.source_n: Systematic review recommendation; no single cohort denominator.
data.quantity: Long-term patient-reported outcome comparison informing operative decisions in older adults
data.source_evidence_basis: The guideline reports strong evidence that surgery does not improve long-term patient-reported outcomes compared with non-operative care for the studied geriatric group, while noting functional demand may explain decisions better than age.
data.limitations: Does not imply surgery is never appropriate; exceptions such as significant deformity or neurologic compromise remain. Age cutoff reflects study conventions and may not match functional age.
data.inferred_scenario_use: Represent age alongside functional demand, deformity, neurologic status, comorbidity, and patient goals; leave final treatment to clinician judgment.
